title: `Link` header parsing too lenient according to RFC 8288
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

https://wpt.fyi/results/preload/preload-referrer-policy.html?label=experimental&label=master&aligned currently passes in all 4 browsers. While working on implementing `rel=preload` in Servo, I was working on parsing `Link` headers. Parsing wasn't working, so I printed the `Link` header used:

```
<http://www1.web-platform.test:8000/preload/resources/echo-referrer.py?uid=0c7238c0-6c5f-49cf-9ad0-694d637de111>;rel="preload";;as="script"
```

Note the double `;;` before `as="script"`. This happens because WPT infrastructure does Python substitution with potentially an empty string:

```python
    response_headers = [(b"Link", b"<%s>;rel=\"preload\";%s;as=\"script\"" %
                        (request.GET.first(b"href", b""),
                         request.GET.first(b"preload-policy", b"")))]

```

Using a Rust crate that implements parsing, I filed an issue: https://github.com/mishazharov/nom-rfc8288/issues/42 However, based on our reading of https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc8288.html#parse-param it seems like `;;` is not allowed. Also looking at the ABNF in https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc8288.html#header

```
  Link       = #link-value
  link-value = "<" URI-Reference ">" *( OWS ";" OWS link-param )
  link-param = token BWS [ "=" BWS ( token / quoted-string ) ]
```

with https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7230.html#section-3.2.6

```
     token          = 1*tchar

     tchar          = "!" / "#" / "$" / "%" / "&" / "'" / "*"
                    / "+" / "-" / "." / "^" / "_" / "`" / "|" / "~"
                    / DIGIT / ALPHA
                    ; any VCHAR, except delimiters
```

Hence `token` must always contain at least 1 character and thus `;;` is disallowed.

Given that all browsers are leniently accepting the `;;`, but it doesn't follow RFC 8288, what is the expected behavior for parsing `Link` headers?
